import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

def fgsm_attack(model, image, label, epsilon=0.1):
    """Generate adversarial example using FGSM."""
    image.requires_grad_(True)
    
    # Forward pass
    output = model(image)
    loss = F.cross_entropy(output, label)
    
    # Backward pass to get input gradients
    model.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    
    # Collect sign of gradient
    data_grad = image.grad.data
    sign_grad = data_grad.sign()
    
    # Create adversarial image
    adv_image = image + epsilon * sign_grad
    
    # Clip to valid range
    adv_image = torch.clamp(adv_image, 0, 1)
    
    return adv_image

# Simple CNN for demonstration
class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(1, 10, kernel_size=5)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(144, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(F.max_pool2d(self.conv(x), 2))
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        return self.fc(x)

# Test FGSM
model = SimpleCNN()
model.eval()

sample_image = torch.rand(1, 1, 28, 28)
sample_label = torch.tensor([3])

# Original prediction
with torch.no_grad():
    original_pred = model(sample_image).argmax(dim=1)

# Generate adversarial example
adv_image = fgsm_attack(model, sample_image, sample_label, epsilon=0.1)

with torch.no_grad():
    adv_pred = model(adv_image).argmax(dim=1)

print(f"Original prediction: {original_pred.item()}")
print(f"Adversarial prediction: {adv_pred.item()}")
print(f"Perturbation norm: {(adv_image - sample_image).abs().max().item():.4f}")
